name: Dockup

modes.label: Native service
modes.note: Hardware and complete resource tariff unverified.

plans.name: Dockup for teams
plans.note: Unlimited users; adds teams/projects, role-based access, custom deployment checklists, reporting and analytics. AWS resource charges are separate.

caveats: YC says ephemeral environments for manual and automated tests. Public pricing returns 404. Current hosted availability and resource price unresolved; not inferred from Active label.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

isolation.quote: EKS runs the Docker images as containers.
isolation.note: Dockup builds your source into Docker images (CodeBuild/ECR) and runs them as containers on AWS EKS in the customer's own AWS account.

image_oci.quote: CodeBuild pulls your source code from Github and builds Docker images. ECR stores the Docker images. EKS runs the Docker images as containers.
image_oci.note: Deploys are Docker/OCI images built from your repo (a Dockerfile you control) and run on EKS; not shown as accepting an arbitrary pre-built image reference directly.

docker_inside.quote: The easiest way to set up and manage deployments on AWS
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Dockup is a CI/CD deploy pipeline onto EKS, not a general-purpose machine you get docker-in-docker access to.

nested_virt.quote: EKS runs the Docker images as containers.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — shared-kernel container isolation on EKS, no /dev/kvm exposed.

desktop.quote: The easiest way to set up and manage deployments on AWS
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Dockup is a deployment automation tool, not a desktop/VNC product.

browser.quote: The easiest way to set up and manage deployments on AWS
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

computer_use.quote: The easiest way to set up and manage deployments on AWS
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

anti_bot.quote: The easiest way to set up and manage deployments on AWS
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no browser/scraping product.

captcha_solving.quote: The easiest way to set up and manage deployments on AWS
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: Dockup uses your cloud infrastructure for deployments and can eject itself on your command.
egress_ip_type.note: Workloads run inside the customer's own AWS account/VPC on EKS, so outbound IPs are standard AWS datacenter IPs.

snapshot.quote: Rolling deployments Dockup deploys your services incrementally with zero downtime
snapshot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — it manages rolling k8s deployments, not VM/disk snapshots.

snapshot_auto.quote: Rolling deployments Dockup deploys your services incrementally with zero downtime
snapshot_auto.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Rolling deployments Dockup deploys your services incrementally with zero downtime
snapshot_on_demand.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

fork.quote: The easiest way to set up and manage deployments on AWS
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no machine-cloning feature described.

fork_running.quote: The easiest way to set up and manage deployments on AWS
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: The easiest way to set up and manage deployments on AWS
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

pause_resume.quote: Auto scaling and load balancing Dockup automatically adds and removes nodes to accommodate varying loads on your applications.
pause_resume.note: not offered: scaling is node add/remove for load, not a pause/resume billing state for a given deployment.

wake_on_request.quote: Auto scaling and load balancing Dockup automatically adds and removes nodes to accommodate varying loads on your applications.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: no sleep/wake-on-request behavior described; deployments run continuously on EKS.

volume_shared.quote: EKS runs the Docker images as containers.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no shared-volume feature described.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Auto scaling and load balancing Dockup automatically adds and removes nodes to accommodate varying loads on your applications.
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: autoscaling responds to load, not idle-based stop/sleep of a given environment.

live_resize.quote: Auto scaling and load balancing Dockup automatically adds and removes nodes to accommodate varying loads on your applications.
live_resize.note: not offered: scaling adds/removes cluster nodes rather than resizing a single running machine's CPU/RAM.

agent_harnesses.quote: Dockup gives on-demand environments for engineering teams so they can merge pull requests with confidence. It works like CircleCI...
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a CI/CD deployment tool, not an AI coding-agent platform.

harness_api.quote: Dockup gives on-demand environments for engineering teams so they can merge pull requests with confidence.
harness_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

own_agent_api.quote: Dockup gives on-demand environments for engineering teams so they can merge pull requests with confidence.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

mcp_server.quote: Dockup gives on-demand environments for engineering teams so they can merge pull requests with confidence.
mcp_server.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no MCP integration described.

lang_python.quote: CodeBuild pulls your source code from Github and builds Docker images.
lang_python.note: not offered: the platform runs whatever your own Dockerfile/source produces; it doesn't itself provide a Python runtime or code-exec SDK.

lang_node.quote: CodeBuild pulls your source code from Github and builds Docker images.
lang_node.note: not offered: same reasoning as lang_python — language support comes from the customer's own Docker image, not a first-party runtime.

ingress_rules.quote: Security groups to lock down your network.
ingress_rules.note: AWS security groups are provisioned by Dockup to control access to exposed resources.

egress_allowlist.quote: VPCs, subnets and forwarding rules for networking rules for your AWS resources. Security groups to lock down your network.
egress_allowlist.note: derived: Dockup provisions VPC/subnet/security-group networking in the customer's AWS account, which functions as egress control, though not explicitly described as an egress allowlist feature.

egress_http_rules.quote: Security groups to lock down your network.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: security groups are IP/port-level (AWS), not HTTP method/path level.

guest_firewall.quote: EKS runs the Docker images as containers.
guest_firewall.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — isolation is shared-kernel containers on EKS, not a full VM/microVM with guest root, so in-guest nftables/iptables control isn't the relevant model.

secret_proxy.quote: IAM permissions for users and AWS resources.
secret_proxy.note: Access model is AWS IAM permissions, not a first-party HTTP credential-injection proxy.

static_egress_ip.quote: VPCs, subnets and forwarding rules for networking rules for your AWS resources.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: no fixed outbound IP feature described; standard AWS networking is provisioned instead.

gpu.quote: The easiest way to set up and manage deployments on AWS
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a web-app deployment/CI tool, no GPU machines described.

windows.quote: EKS runs the Docker images as containers.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Linux container deployments on EKS, no Windows machines described.

macos.quote: EKS runs the Docker images as containers.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no macOS machines described.

self_host.quote: Sign up and connect your Github and AWS accounts
self_host.note: Dockup is a hosted SaaS control plane that provisions resources into the customer's own AWS account; the Dockup software/control-plane itself is not self-hostable per available docs.

open_source.note: No open-source license or public source repo mentioned anywhere on the marketing site.

eu_data_residency.quote: Dockup uses your cloud infrastructure for deployments and can eject itself on your command.
eu_data_residency.note: derived: resources are provisioned into the customer's own AWS account/region, which the customer can choose to be an EU AWS region.

max_session_h.quote: EKS runs the Docker images as containers.
max_session_h.note: Deployed services run continuously on EKS until redeployed/torn down — not a time-boxed sandbox session model.

ssh.quote: Behind the scenes, Dockup automatically creates these AWS resources for your deployments: CodeBuild pulls your source code from Github and builds Docker images. ECR stores the Docker images. EKS runs the Docker images as containers.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Dockup is a Github-to-AWS/EKS deployment automation tool (push to deploy, checklists, rollbacks); it does not give users a shell/SSH into the underlying containers or nodes

persistent_disk.quote: EKS runs the Docker images as containers.
persistent_disk.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Dockup deploys stateless containerized services onto EKS; it exposes no persistent-disk feature of its own (any storage is via the customer's own AWS resources, not a Dockup feature)

volume_attach.quote: EKS runs the Docker images as containers.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no volume-attach capability is described; Dockup only automates build/deploy of containers onto AWS, not storage management

public_ipv4.quote: VPCs, subnets and forwarding rules for networking rules for your AWS resources. Security groups to lock down your network. ... SSL Dockup automatically provisions and renews SSL certificates.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Dockup fronts deployed services with load balancing/SSL over HTTPS rather than exposing a public IPv4 per machine
